stem: Why is a representative delivery check required after routine system execution?
choices: It mainly helps estimate eventual crop yield after irrigation.
Controller or pump status confirms that the system was commanded to run, but representative checks are needed to verify that solution actually reached required crop locations.
It replaces the work order because field delivery is more important than planned instructions.
It reveals the exact nutrient composition delivered at every emitter.
rationale: A controller can show that a command was issued and equipment may show that it operated, but neither proves that every required location received solution. Clogged emitters, pressure loss, closed valves, leaks, or line problems can create delivery failures. Representative checks verify actual outcome rather than assuming command equals delivery.
